mainTopic: Reassembling a collapsible bed, catching lamp sparks on שבת, and the opening of במה טומנין (materials for wrapping food)
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about putting together a bed made of separate parts. The תנא קמא forbids it, and fastening the parts tightly counts as Torah-level בונה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits it if the parts fit loosely, and in a story about a bed in רב חמא's house, רבא says he follows that view. A new משנה then permits placing a vessel under a lamp to catch sparks, but forbids putting water in it, because the water puts the sparks out. The גמרא explains that the vessel does not become unusable, because sparks have no real substance. It also asks whether the ban on water follows רבי יוסי's view on indirect extinguishing. It rejects that idea, and רב אשי explains that even the רבנן forbid it, because the water speeds up the extinguishing. After the הדרן for פרק כירה, the new chapter במה טומנין lists materials one may not wrap food in, some forbidden always and some only when moist. The גמרא asks whether the forbidden גפת means olive or sesame residue, tries a proof from רבי זירא, and begins rejecting it. That rejection continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Reassembling the bed is forbidden, and fastening it tightly is a Torah violation
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its ruling: loosely putting the bed back together is exempt but still forbidden, and fastening it tightly makes one liable to a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is forbidden. And one may not fasten it tightly, and if he did fasten it, he is liable to bring a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that started on the previous amud, about putting a bed made of parts back together on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling has two levels. Simply fitting the parts back together is פטור אבל אסור: there is no Torah punishment, but the רבנן forbid it. Fastening the parts tightly counts as real building (בונה), so one who does it brings a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt from punishment, but still forbidden (rabbinically)
Fasten or drive in tightly
Liable to bring a sin-offering (a Torah-level violation done by mistake)
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The words אבל אסור continue a sentence on the previous amud. The earlier part said reassembling the bed is פטור. So 'but it is forbidden' means forbidden only מדרבנן, not a Torah prohibition.

phrases.english: But it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: This finishes the earlier part of the ברייתא that said 'he is exempt.'

phrases.english: And he may not fasten it tightly,
and if he fastened it, he is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Loose reassembly: rabbinically forbidden. Tight fastening: Torah-level בונה, liable to a חטאת.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits reassembly if the parts are loose
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees and says that if the parts fit loosely, putting them together is completely permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: If it was loose, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the same ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits reassembling the bed when its parts fit loosely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbade loose reassembly מדרבנן. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל removes even that rabbinic prohibition when the parts are רפוי, because loose fitting is not like building at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Loose; parts that fit together easily without force
Permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the opinion רבא relies on in the story that comes next.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
If it was loose, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reassembling loose parts is permitted even מדרבנן.

steps.title: A collapsible bed was reassembled on יום טוב in רב חמא's house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells a story: in רב חמא's house, a collapsible bed was put back together on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the house of רב חמא there was a collapsible bed. They would reassemble it on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a practical case of the ברייתא. A bed made of parts was put together on יום טוב, which seems to go against the תנא קמא's rabbinic prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: The house of רב חמא (רבא's grandfather)
A collapsible bed made of separate parts
They would put it back together
יום טוב, a festival day

phrases.english: In the house of Rav Chama
there was a collapsible bed.
They would reassemble it on Yom Tov.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּי רַב חָמָא הֲוָה מִטָּה גְּלָלְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא to a real case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, a collapsible bed was reassembled on יום טוב.

steps.title: A scholar challenges רבא: even if it is atypical building, it is still rabbinically forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A scholar asks רבא how this is allowed. Even if it is only בנין מן הצד, so there is no Torah prohibition, there is still a rabbinic one.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Sages said to רבא: What is your thinking? That it is building in an atypical way? Granted there is no Torah prohibition, but there is at least a rabbinic prohibition!
steps.whatsHappening: A scholar challenges רבא about the practice in his family's house. He guesses רבא's reason and shows that it is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholar assumes רבא thinks loose reassembly is only בנין מן הצד, which takes away the Torah prohibition. But according to the תנא קמא in the ברייתא, it is still אסור מדרבנן, so the practice looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain one of the scholars
What is your reasoning?
Building done in an unusual, indirect way
Granted, even if
There is at least a rabbinic prohibition

phrases.english: One of the Sages said to Rava:
What is your thinking?
That it is building in an atypical way?
Granted that there is no Torah prohibition,
there is at least a rabbinic prohibition!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִדְּרַבָּנַן לְרָבָא מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice described in the story
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of reassembling the bed on יום טוב in רב חמא's house
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Avoiding the Torah prohibition is not enough. According to the תנא קמא, a rabbinic prohibition still remains.

steps.title: רבא answers that he follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that he holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who permits reassembly completely when the parts are loose.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I hold like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who said: If it was loose, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by saying which תנא he follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depended on the תנא קמא's rabbinic prohibition. רבא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who permits loose reassembly with no prohibition at all, so the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: I hold, I am of the opinion
In accordance with

steps.whatToRemember: A loose collapsible bed: the תנא קמא forbids reassembling it מדרבנן, but רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits it, and רבא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in practice.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סְבִירָא לִי
phrases.english: I hold in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
who said: If it was loose, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סְבִירָא לִי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Following a different תנא (siding with the dissenting opinion)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The scholar assumed רבא follows the תנא קמא and relies only on בנין מן הצד.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so loose reassembly is fully permitted.

steps.title: משנה: a vessel may be placed under a lamp to catch sparks, but no water may be put in it
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: one may put a vessel under a lamp to catch falling sparks, but may not put water in it, because that would put out the sparks.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We may place a vessel under the lamp to catch sparks, but one may not put water into it, because he would be extinguishing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: catching sparks from a burning lamp on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Catching sparks is allowed because it only stops them from causing damage. Water is forbidden because the sparks would be put out by it, which is כיבוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Sparks (burning drops of oil falling from the lamp)
Extinguishes, the מלאכה of כיבוי

phrases.english: MISHNAH: We may place a vessel beneath the lamp
to catch sparks,
but he may not put water into it
because he would be extinguishing.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹתְנִין כְּלִי תַּחַת הַנֵּר לְקַבֵּל נִיצוֹצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Catching sparks in an empty vessel is permitted. Putting water in the vessel is forbidden because of כיבוי.

steps.title: The vessel seems to become unusable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: by placing a vessel where מוקצה sparks will fall into it, isn't one making the vessel unusable, which is forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't he negating the vessel from its readiness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's permission to put a vessel under the lamp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sparks are מוקצה. Once they land in the vessel, the vessel can no longer be moved. Making a usable vessel unusable on שבת, called מבטל כלי מהיכנו, is forbidden, so how can the משנה allow it?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that (opens a challenge)
Making a vessel lose its readiness for use on שבת
Something set aside that may not be moved on שבת

phrases.english: GEMARA: But isn't he negating
the vessel from its readiness?!

steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to place a vessel under the lamp
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מוקצה sparks would make the vessel unmovable, and that is the forbidden act of מבטל כלי מהיכנו.

steps.title: Sparks have no substance
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that sparks have no real substance, so the vessel does not become מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: Sparks have no substance.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sparks burn out right away and leave nothing real in the vessel. Since nothing מוקצה stays inside it, the vessel remains usable and movable, so it was never made unusable.

keyTerms.meaning: They have no real substance

steps.whatToRemember: Placing a vessel under sparks is not מבטל כלי מהיכנו, because sparks vanish and leave nothing מוקצה behind.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Sparks have no substance.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the facts: the sparks never create a real מוקצה presence
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sparks would rest in the vessel and make it מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sparks vanish right away, so the vessel stays usable and nothing is made unusable.

steps.title: Does the anonymous משנה follow רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on putting water in the vessel and suggests it follows רבי יוסי, who forbids גורם לכיבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And he may not put water into it, because he puts out the sparks.' Shall we say we learned this anonymous משנה like רבי יוסי, who said that causing a fire to go out indirectly is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the second half of the משנה (no water in the vessel). It asks whether this unnamed ruling quietly follows the opinion of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting water in the vessel does not put out any spark directly. The spark goes out by itself when it falls in. Elsewhere רבי יוסי forbids this kind of indirect extinguishing and the רבנן permit it, so the גמרא suggests the משנה must follow רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggested inference)
An anonymous, unattributed ruling in a משנה
Causing a fire to go out indirectly
Extinguishes, puts out a fire

steps.confusionAlert: Here the גמרא is only suggesting that the משנה follows רבי יוסי. It is not a conclusion, and the next steps reject it.

phrases.english: And he may not put water into it
because he extinguishes.
Shall we say we learned an anonymous ruling like Rabbi Yosei,
who said causing extinguishing is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first half of the משנה (the vessel itself) to the second half (no water).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's ban on water reflects רבי יוסי's view that indirect extinguishing is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יוסי only forbade it on שבת itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: רבי יוסי forbids indirect extinguishing only when the act is done on שבת, not on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? Granted, רבי יוסי said it is forbidden on שבת. Did he say it is forbidden on ערב שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 9. It points out that רבי יוסי's ban was about acting on שבת itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה seems to forbid putting the water in even before שבת starts. רבי יוסי never said that setting things up before שבת is forbidden. So his view cannot explain our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really think so? (a rejection formula)
Say / granted that
Friday, before שבת begins

phrases.english: And can you really think so?
Say that Rabbi Yosei said it on Shabbat;
did he say it on Shabbat eve?

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי's ban is limited to acting on שבת, while the משנה applies even to ערב שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the water is forbidden even before שבת
steps.stepSummary: One might say the משנה only talks about placing water on שבת. A ברייתא blocks this, because it explicitly forbids the water even from ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too it means on שבת, but a ברייתא taught: One may put a vessel under a lamp to catch sparks on שבת, and needless to say on ערב שבת. And one may not put water into it, because he puts them out, even from ערב שבת, and needless to say on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shuts down a possible defense of the רבי יוסי reading. It brings a ברייתא that states clearly that putting in the water is forbidden even before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could say the משנה only means placing water on שבת, which would fit רבי יוסי. But the ברייתא says the water is forbidden 'from ערב שבת.' Since רבי יוסי does not forbid pre-שבת setups, the reason for the ban must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible defense)
Sparks
It goes without saying

steps.confusionAlert: The two halves of the ברייתא run in opposite directions. The vessel is allowed even on שבת, so of course on ערב שבת. The water is forbidden even on ערב שבת, so of course on שבת.

phrases.english: And if you say here too it is on Shabbat,
but it was taught in a baraita:
One may place a vessel under the lamp
to catch sparks on Shabbat,
and needless to say on Shabbat eve.
And he may not put water into it
because he extinguishes,
even from Shabbat eve,
and needless to say on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי בְּשַׁבָּת, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible defense against step 10 and so strengthens the rejection.
steps.raayaObject: That the water is forbidden even when placed before שבת, which רבי יוסי's view cannot explain.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating the water is forbidden from ערב שבת.

steps.title: רב אשי: even the רבנן agree, because the water speeds up the extinguishing
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the ban fits even the רבנן, because water makes the sparks go out immediately. That is more than ordinary indirect causation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: Even if you say it follows the רבנן, here is different, because he brings its extinguishing closer.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the רבי יוסי explanation failed, רב אשי gives a new reason for the משנה. It works even according to the רבנן, who usually allow indirect extinguishing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ordinary גורם לכיבוי, the fire only goes out later, once it reaches the barrier. Here the spark dies the moment it lands in the water. Because the water speeds up the extinguishing so directly, even the רבנן forbid it, and it does not matter when the water was put in.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say it follows the Sages
Here is different
Brings its extinguishing closer / speeds it up

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on putting water under a lamp is not about רבי יוסי's view on indirect extinguishing. According to everyone it is forbidden, because water speeds up the extinguishing (מקרב את כיבויו).
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical line: indirect causing of extinguishing may be allowed according to the רבנן, but speeding it up directly is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Even if you say it follows the Rabbis,
here it is different,
because he hastens its extinguishing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected רבי יוסי explanation with a new reason that everyone accepts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on water seemed to depend on רבי יוסי's strict view about גורם לכיבוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the רבנן forbid it, because the water speeds up the sparks going out.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק כירה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter of כירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter כירה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the third chapter of שבת, פרק כירה. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן formula expresses the learner's wish to come back and review the chapter. Everything after this line begins a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (closing formula for a chapter)
A small stove; the name of the chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, Kirah

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion.

steps.title: New משנה: materials you may not wrap food in, wet or dry
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter opens by asking in what one may and may not wrap a pot to keep it warm. It lists materials forbidden whether moist or dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: In what may one wrap food, and in what may one not wrap it? One may not wrap it in pressed residue (גפת), nor in manure, nor in salt, nor in lime, nor in sand, whether moist or dry.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter (במה טומנין) begins. Its first משנה lists materials that may not be used to wrap a pot of food before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טמינה means wrapping a pot in material so it keeps its heat. The materials listed here give off heat by themselves, so they actually add heat to the pot. That is like cooking, so they are forbidden whether wet or dry.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Wrapping/insulating food to keep it warm (טמינה)
Solid residue left after pressing produce for oil (the גמרא asks in step 16 whether olive or sesame residue is meant)
Manure
Lime
Moist and dry

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about putting a pot on a fire. It is about wrapping it in material. The problem is that these specific materials add heat instead of only keeping heat in.

phrases.english: MISHNA: In what may one insulate
and in what may one not insulate?
One may not insulate in pressed residue
nor in manure,
nor in salt, nor in lime,
nor in sand,
whether moist or dry.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בַּמֶּה טוֹמְנִין וּבַמָּה אֵין טוֹמְנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not wrap food in pressed residue (גפת), manure, salt, lime, or sand, whether moist or dry, because they add heat.

steps.title: Materials forbidden only when moist
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists a second group of materials (straw, grape skins, soft fibers, grasses). One may not wrap food in them while they are moist, but one may once they are dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not wrap food in straw, grape skins, soft fibers, or grasses while they are moist. But one may wrap food in them when they are dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list. Now it gives materials that are forbidden only when they are wet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first group (from Step 14) was forbidden whether moist or dry, because those materials always produce heat. This second group produces heat only when moist, so the ban depends on their condition. Once dry, they just hold in warmth and do not add heat.

keyTerms.meaning: Straw
Grape skins or pits left after pressing
Soft fibers or rags
Moist, wet
Dry

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two lists. The first list is forbidden always. This list is forbidden only while wet.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two categories: materials forbidden whether moist or dry, and materials forbidden only when moist.

phrases.english: And not in straw, and not in grape skins
and not in soft fibers, and not in grasses
at a time when they are moist
but one may insulate in them when they are dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה begun in Step 14 by adding the second category of materials.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Straw, grape skins, soft fibers, and grasses are forbidden for הטמנה only when moist and are permitted when dry.

steps.title: Olive residue or sesame residue?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה's גפת means olive residue, which would leave sesame residue permitted. Or does it mean sesame residue, so that olive residue is forbidden all the more?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Did the משנה mean olive residue, so sesame residue is fine? Or did it mean sesame residue, and olive residue is forbidden all the more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking which kind of גפת the משנה is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Olive residue gives off more heat than sesame residue. If the משנה meant olives, the weaker sesame residue might be allowed. If the משנה meant sesame, then the hotter olive residue is surely forbidden through a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (a real dilemma)
Pressed residue left after extracting oil
Sesame seeds
It is fine, permitted
All the more so

phrases.english: GEMARA: A dilemma was raised before them:
Did we learn about the residue of olives,
but the residue of sesame is fine?
Or perhaps we learned about sesame residue
and all the more so olive residue?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the term גפת from the first list of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's גפת refers to olive residue only, or to sesame residue (and therefore olives too).

steps.title: Proof from placing a basket on olive residue
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא, quoting a sage from the school of רבי ינאי, says a basket of wrapped food may not be placed on olive residue. The גמרא concludes that the משנה must have meant olive residue.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי זירא said in the name of one of the school of רבי ינאי: A basket in which one wrapped food may not be placed on olive residue. Learn from this that the משנה meant olive residue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement to try to answer the question from Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement mentions only olive residue as the forbidden heat source. The גמרא infers that the משנה's גפת also means olives. That would imply sesame residue is permitted.

steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's גפת means olive residue, so sesame residue is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי זירא's statement in the name of the school of רבי ינאי about placing a basket on olive residue.

steps.title: Wrapping in it differs from placing on it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. For actual wrapping, even sesame residue is forbidden. The statement about olives refers to a different case, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, I can tell you that for wrapping, sesame residue is also forbidden. But regarding...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says רבי זירא's statement does not settle what the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Placing a basket on top of residue is a milder case than burying food inside it. So רבי זירא may name only olives for the placing case. Meanwhile, the משנה's ban on wrapping could still include sesame. The sentence continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, I can tell you (introduces a rejection)
Regarding the matter of
Wrapping or burying food to keep it warm
Also

steps.confusionAlert: Wrapping food inside residue (הטמנה) and placing a basket on top of residue are two different cases. The rejection depends on this difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 17 by separating wrapping from placing on top.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference from רבי זירא's statement to the meaning of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The statement concerns placing a basket on residue, which is a milder case. It cannot show that sesame residue is permitted for actual wrapping.
